concepts.def: Born around 570 CE and orphaned young, Muhammad was raised by his grandfather and uncle, worked as a trader, and earned the name al-Amin, 'the trustworthy'.
In about 610 CE, in the cave of Hira, Muslims believe the angel Jibril commanded Muhammad to 'Recite!', beginning the revelation of the Qur'an.
The Quraysh met his preaching with ridicule, boycott and persecution; the deaths of Khadijah and Abu Talib made one year the 'Year of Sorrow'.
Muslims believe the Prophet journeyed by night to Jerusalem and ascended through the heavens, where the five daily prayers were given.
After the Hijrah in 622 he led the new community, made treaties, survived battles, and returned to take Makkah peacefully in 630.
His farewell sermon in 632 stressed equality and good treatment of others; he died that year, honoured as the final prophet and the best example for Muslims.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Islam: The Life & Importance of the Prophet Muhammad — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Islam: The Life & Importance of the Prophet Muhammad brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Islam: The Life & Importance of the Prophet Muhammad.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which angel do Muslims believe brought the first revelation in the cave of Hira?
options: Jibril
Mika'il
Israfil
Izra'il

mcqs.q: What name did Muhammad earn in Makkah for his honesty?
options: Al-Amin, 'the trustworthy'
Al-Faruq
Al-Siddiq
Al-Khalil

mcqs.q: Who was Muhammad's first wife and earliest supporter?
options: Khadijah
Aisha
Fatimah
Hafsa

mcqs.q: Why is Muhammad called the 'Seal of the Prophets'?
options: Muslims believe he is the final prophet, completing the line of prophets
He sealed his letters with a special ring only
He was the first prophet ever sent
He sealed the doors of the Ka'bah

mcqs.q: Do Muslims worship the Prophet Muhammad?
options: Muhammad conquered Makkah before receiving any revelations.
Muslims worship the cave of Hira where revelation began.
Muslims worship Muhammad in the way Christians worship Jesus.
No - worship in Islam is for Allah alone; Muhammad is revered as the final messenger and the best example to follow, which is why the old label 'Mohammedanism' is rejected.

mcqs.q: Did Muhammad compose the Qur'an himself?
options: Muhammad sat down and wrote the Qur'an as his own book.
The Qur'an was discovered already written inside the Ka'bah.
Muslims believe the Qur'an is the word of Allah revealed through the angel Jibril over about twenty-three years; tradition describes Muhammad as unlettered, with scribes recording the revelations.
Muhammad conquered Makkah before receiving any revelations.

mcqs.q: Did Muhammad spread Islam in Makkah by military force?
options: Muslims worship the cave of Hira where revelation began.
No - for about thirteen years in Makkah the Muslims were a persecuted minority preaching peacefully, and even the later capture of Makkah in 630 was largely bloodless, with a general amnesty.
Islam was spread in Makkah from the start by the sword.
Muhammad conquered Makkah before receiving any revelations.
